stories.headline: Trump signals possible new strikes on Iran as conflict threatens to widen

sources.body: Reports claim that the US and Israel have ramped up military drills and planned new strikes in Iran, potentially targeting energy sites, drone facilities and missile arsenals. Details by FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem, Noga Tarnopolsky.
sources.headline: Reports show US and Israel are planning new strikes on Iran

sources.body:
The US has pushed back on the IRGC’s claims, dismissing them as an attempt to increase oil prices ahead of US elections.

Iran says that seven oil tankers have been struck and sustained damage in the Strait of Hormuz, the largest single-day toll for the waterway since the United States and Israel started their war against Iran on February 28.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said in a statement on Thursday that four of the vessels were transferring oil when they were targeted and caught fire overnight. The other three were disabled after striking mines.

The claims could not be independently verified, and the report did not provide details about possible casualties or the tankers’ flags.

The IRGC also warned that it could strike US bases across the Middle East if Washington moves to help tankers transit other parts of the strait.

“The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the IRGC said in a statement on its Sepah News website. “This is a serious warning.”

Iran claims control over Hormuz, a strategic shipping route through which one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies passed before war broke out. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation.

But the US military has been escorting vessels through the waterway in increasing numbers, with Iran responding by stepping up attacks.

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that “Iran is doing everything they can to drive up the price of oil prior to the US Midterm Election”.

In a post on his Truth Social platform, he added: “They are making up fake hits, mines, and everything else because more oil is coming through the Hormuz Strait now than it did even prior to the beginning of the conflict.”

A US Central Command spokesperson, speaking anonymously to Al Jazeera, also called Iran’s mine claims incorrect.

The spokesperson said US forces have cleared the international shipping lanes of mines and that Iran is using missiles and drones.

The strait remains open, the spokesperson said, with 95 percent of vessels getting through.

The attacks, the spokesperson added, show Tehran’s “desperation” under the US blockade, which cuts Iran off from the resources it needs to rebuild the military capabilities the US has said it destroyed.

“The number of ships and tankers attacked every single day is increasing, and Iran is saying it is continuing to do this because they are not going to allow any change in that situation,” said Al Jazeera’s Mohamed Vall, reporting from Tehran.

“They have full control over the Strait of Hormuz right now, they say.”

Vall said there is also talk in Tehran about an imminent escalation in the war, with the Iranians expecting the US to attack even before US midterm elections in early November.

“The IRGC army chief has boasted that Iran is more ready than anytime before, and has produced enough weapons and equipment to wage a symmetrical war against the United States,” he said.

Reporting from the US White House, Al Jazeera’s Kimberly Halkett said: “Striking Iran does not appear to serve any Republican interests”, adding that pre-election polls tell the same story for Trump’s political party.
sources.headline: Iran says seven ships hit in Hormuz Strait, warns US of wider response

stories.headline: Magnitude-7 earthquake in Tibet kills at least 16 and destroys hundreds of homes

sources.body:
Several survivors of the earthquake have told local media about their harrowing escape from the tremor.

Speaking to Tibet Daily, Nagqu resident Yixi Cuomu said she was asleep in her bed when her house started shaking violently. Realising it was an earthquake, she headed outside barefoot, "her legs trembling uncontrollably" as she descended the staircase in her home.

Another eyewitness said the shaking was so violent "that in that moment I felt as if several hundred yaks were running past us".

Residents chose to spend the night in subzero temperatures, seeking shelter in tents or their cars, as they feared further aftershocks could trap them in their homes, according to the news outlet.
sources.headline: Powerful earthquake hits Tibet, killing 16 people, reports say

sources.body:
Search and rescue efforts under way after quake strikes region’s north, officials say, while at least seven aftershocks recorded

A magnitude-7 earthquake has hit China’s Tibet region, killing at least 16 people, injuring 54 and collapsing hundreds of homes in the northern regional city of Nagqu, official media said.

Search and rescue efforts continued after the collapse of at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials.

More than 1,600 people from the local county were deployed for rescue efforts. Supplies including 1,000 prefabricated housing units and about 3,000 tents and folding beds as well as torches and winter clothing arrived in the region.

The US Geological Survey said the quake occurred at 10.33pm local time on Thursday, with its epicentre 191km (119 miles) east-northeast of Nagqu, in a sparsely populated, high-altitude area of northern Tibet . It put the earthquake’s depth at 18km.

The US agency recorded at least seven aftershocks with magnitude between 4.3 and 5.2, all of them with a depth of 10km, according to its website.

Videos posted by China’s national broadcaster CCTV said showed workers running out of restaurants and objects falling off shelves at supermarkets when the quake struck.

China’s official Xinhua news agency said on Friday that communication in some areas hit by the quake was down. Local railway authorities had taken emergency actions to halt trains passing through the region.

More than 300 police officers had been dispatched for relief work while the regional fire and rescue corps has mobilised almost 350 personnel to the affected areas, Xinhua reported.

Rescue workers clambered through damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs, footage on CCTV showed.

The earthquake also caused rockfalls that had forced local authorities to close a section of national highway 317, allowing only emergency, rescue and official support vehicles through as crews worked to clear debris, according to Xinhua.

Intermittent snows were expected in the quake region over the next three days, Xinhua said. It was the biggest quake in the region in the past five years, CCTV said.

China’s leader, Xi Jinping, called for all-out efforts in rescue operations and medical relief work.

Nagqu is more than 300km north of Tibet’s capital, Lhasa.

Earthquakes are relatively common in China. In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in one in Tibet’s rural Tingri county.

In December 2023, a quake in remote Gansu province in north-west China killed at least 134 people, state media said. That quake was China’s deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people died in the south-western province of Yunnan.

A huge tremor in Sichuan province in 2008 left approximately 90,000 people dead or missing, including about 5,000 schoolchildren.
sources.headline: Magnitude-7 earthquake hits China’s Tibet, killing at least 16 and destroying hundreds of homes

sources.body: At least 16 people have died and dozens more have been injured after a major earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale shook China’s remote Tibet region on Thursday, state media said. Hundreds of houses collapsed in the tremor.
sources.headline: Strong earthquake strikes China’s remote Tibet region

stories.headline: BBC investigation finds Sudan’s RSF fighters deliberately targeted hospitals

sources.body:
A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago.

UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes.

The paramilitary group's health minister described the allegations as propaganda and a deliberate attempt by the national army and its allies to smear the RSF's reputation.

Using sources who were on the ground in el-Fasher, the BBC has found details of at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites from May 2024 to October 2025 - some hit multiple times.

Under international law it is illegal to attack health facilities or their staff during conflict.

The investigation also reveals the toll on medical workers in the western city. In the period from April 2023 to October 2025, the BBC's data shows 120 were injured, 55 killed and 10 forcibly "disappeared" or abducted.

"The RSF [were] trying to evacuate the hospitals, to put them out of service because the health system is the cornerstone of any city or any state," says Dr Muhamed Suliman, a surgeon who was based in el-Fasher during the siege and spoke to the BBC.

"The RSF started hitting these areas so citizens have no longer any way to stay there. It was intense. It was deliberate. It was planned."

The investigation comes a year after the fall of el-Fasher, one of the most brutal chapters of the civil war which erupted in April 2023 between the RSF and Sudan's military.

Both sides have been accused of attacks on health facilities.

In March 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the bombing of al-Daein hospital in RSF-held eastern Darfur, which killed dozens and forced the site to close. Sudan's military is believed to have carried out the drone strikes, although it has denied responsibility.

But events in el-Fasher represent "one of the clearest and most severe examples of the wider impact of the conflict on health care in Sudan," the WHO said in response to a BBC query.

UN investigators have reported that the fighting in el-Fasher bore the "hallmarks of genocide", where historical ethnic animosities have seen Arab militias - now the backbone of RSF forces - target non-Arab groups such as those that populate the city.

The BBC's investigation reveals for the first time a detailed chronology of attacks on healthcare during the long siege of the city.

Some medical facilities in el-Fasher closed down within weeks of the country's civil war starting in April 2023.

Crucially this included one of the main hospitals - the Teaching Hospital - located in a conflict zone in the middle of the city.

Its operations were moved to el-Fasher's South Hospital. There medical services continued, although increasingly hindered by power cuts and dwindling supplies.
sources.headline: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC investigation finds

stories.headline: Brazil’s presidential runoff remains too close to call as Lula faces Flávio Bolsonaro

sources.body: Brazil's future within the margin of error ahead of Sunday's presidential runoff: most of the latest polls put the far-right's Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva... a lead that's narrowed after last weekend's acrimomious debate.
sources.headline: Back to the Bolsonaros? Brazil presidential run-off goes down to the wire

sources.body:
El presidente de Brasil, Lula da Silva, saluda a sus seguidores a su llegada a un mitin en la ciudad de Belo Horizonte este miércoles. 

En una recta final llena de suspenso a tres días de las elecciones presidenciales brasileñas, la ventaja de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre el acgual presidente Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, se estrecha cada vez más y todo apunta a un empate técnico el próximo domingo.

Según la encuesta más reciente -de la empresa Quaest y realizada en parte después del tenso debate en televisión del pasado domingo-, la ventaja del candidato de la extrema derecha, hijo del expresidente actualmente en régimen de prisión domiciliaria, ha bajado de dos puntos a solo uno en la última semana. Según otra nueva encuesta de BTG/Mexus, Flávio rebasa a Lula por solo 0,6 puntos decimales. En la tarde del jueves, otra encuesta importante como la de Datafolha mostró como Lula y Bolsonaro están igualados en el 50%. Hace una semana, el segundo ganaba por tres puntos en la misma encuesta.

En estos momentos Lula tiene el impulso a su favor, dicen los politólogos, en una campaña dinamizada por las manifestaciones masivas del pasado fin de semana y por una entrada tarde pero eficaz en redes sociales. Lula, a los 80 años, ha descubierto un don para los vídeos selfi siguiendo los consejos del mayor gurú de redes en la izquierda brasileña, André Janones, actualmente recuperándose de un ataque de arritmia cardíaca sufrido tras debate el domingo.

No cabe duda de que estas elecciones son de infarto tanto por la proximidad de los dos candidatos como por lo que se juega. Flávio Bolsonaro representa una nueva derecha populista ascendente en América latina, que muestra poco respeto por la democracia o por la verdad, con estrechos lazos con la Casa Blanca de Donald Trump.

Lula representa una vieja izquierda que, pese a sus logros en combatir la pobreza, provoca un rechazo visceral en una parte amplia de la clase media brasileña, así como entre los que el sociólogo Jessé Souza califica como los “pobres de derecha”.

Un importante dato en la encuesta de Quaest es que el rechazo a Lula ha disminuido del 52% al 47%. Bajar este elevado nivel de desaprobación se consideraba un sine qua non de un posible sorpasso por parte del viejo líder del Partido de los Trabajadores. Mientras, el rechazo a Flávio Bolsonaro sube. Aunque la actuación de Lula en el debate ha sido criticada, hay un consenso de que Flávio fue percibido como demasiado agresivo. El estrechamiento de la ventaja del candidato de la derecha “tiene menos que ver con Lula que con el rechazo a Flávio”, dijo un analista en Río.

La segunda irrupción de Javier Milei en la campaña, al igual que en España, ha sido otra ayuda a Lula, según los comentaristas. Milei, despotricó el martes contra “el ladrón izquierdista” que puede “robar las elecciones” y fue reprochado por la Cancillería brasileña. No es casualidad que Bolsonaro ya haya dejado de poner la motosierra de Milei como ejemplo. El antes candidato fiscalmente responsable ha anunciado en los últimos días su apoyo a medidas de gasto público, siguiendo a Lula, que ha subido subsidios, los precios y los combustibles. Es lo que se califica ya en el análisis electoral como una “subasta populista”. Eso sí, los mercados no han reaccionado negativamente a la nueva laxitud fiscal de Flávio, una señal de que cuentan con que sus promesas no se cumplan.
sources.headline: Las encuestas confirman el empate técnico entre Lula y Bolsonaro a tres días de las elecciones

sources.body:
Our Latin America correspondent, Tom Phillips, heads to Roraima to hear what’s at stake for the rainforest and the communities that live there in the Brazilian presidential runoff on Sunday. Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.com

For the Amazon and the communities who live there, the stakes in Sunday’s Brazilian presidential election runoff could scarcely be higher.

Our Latin America correspondent, Tom Phillips heads to Roraima, the country’s most northern state, to hear from voters, preachers and politicians in a region that heavily backed Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round.

He finds them all hopeful that the far-right candidate will bring back the mining that his father Jair so heartily encouraged when in power in an administration that oversaw the felling of 11m acres (4.5m hectares) of rainforest.

Tom also meets Indigenous activists determined to fight back even if the Bolsonaros take power again.

Helen Pidd asks what it will all mean, not only for Brazil but also for the climate crisis more broadly.
sources.headline: Brazil’s election and the battle for the Amazon – podcast

stories.headline: Venezuelans hold their first nationwide protest in nearly two years, demanding elections

sources.body:
No date has been set to decide on a successor for Nicolas Maduro after the former president was captured by US forces.

Thousands of Venezuelans have taken to the streets in several cities to demand free elections and other political changes, in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years.

US President Donald Trump and acting President Delcy Rodriguez have said there would be elections, but no date has been set for a vote to decide on a successor for Nicolas Maduro, after the former Venezuelan president was captured by US forces in a military raid in January.

Opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner Maria Corina Machado, who has been outside the country for nearly a year after living in hiding following a contested 2024 election, has said elections must take place by July 2027.

Her Vente Venezuela movement organised the protest, which took place in the capital Caracas and other cities, including Valencia, Maracay, San Cristobal and Maracaibo.

“Seeing this makes me happy because I know change is possible,” said 18-year-old cosmetology student Leosmary Hernandez, as she gathered with hundreds of others in northern Maracay. “I’ve been through so many hardships, so many problems because of the dollar, and difficulties studying. I have high hopes for my country and for our next leader and president, Maria Corina.”

“I went out to protest before, when things were much tougher, and I’m even less afraid today because I want my voice to be heard,” she added.

Since January 3, the country has been led by interim President Delcy Rodriguez of the long-governing United Socialist Party of Venezuela (PSUV).

PSUV leaders have been accused of carrying out human rights abuses against political dissidents, including arbitrary arrest, imprisonment and torture.

After the United States launched a military operation to abduct and jail former President Nicolas Maduro, the PSUV remained in power with the support of the White House.

US President Trump has backed Rodriguez’s leadership, despite her having been Maduro’s vice president.

His administration has maintained an active role in Venezuela, exerting control over its oil resources and pressuring the Rodriguez government for reforms.

Venezuela’s socialist movement, in power since 1999 under late President Hugo Chavez and then Maduro, has in the past deployed security forces against protesters, but government forces had minimal presence at protest sites on Thursday, and in many smaller cities demonstrators dispersed before dark.

The ruling Socialist Party called for its supporters to march from Caracas’ Plaza Venezuela, the same place the opposition planned to gather two hours later, to a location near the presidential palace to commemorate Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello, known for his close ties to the security services, was pictured on state television attending the march, while the opposition supporters moved their protest to a nearby location.

Talks between a faction of the opposition and the interim government , aimed at remaking the top court and the electoral council ahead of eventual elections, held their latest session this month, but changes could take significant time.
sources.headline: Venezuelans demand elections in first national protest in nearly two years

stories.headline: Democrats’ top Senate super PAC reports record $354 million fundraising haul

sources.body: Democrats’ top Senate-focused super PAC will report raising $354 million through Oct. 14 — including roughly $88 million in the first two weeks of the month— as Democrats race to seize control of the upper chamber in the election’s closing weeks. Senate Majority PAC shared their fundraising totals, which are higher than any previous cycle, with POLITICO ahead of a Federal Election Commission deadline later Thursday. The super PAC had $32.7 million in the bank as of Oct. 14. “This is already the strongest cycle in Senate Majority PAC’s history, and it’s arriving exactly when it counts,” SMP spokesperson Lauren French said in a statement. “We’re on the air across the battleground through Election Day, and every dollar is going toward beating price-gouging Republicans and winning back the Senate.” That’s more than the $306 million SMP raised in the 2024 campaign cycle, according to FEC filings , its previous high. SMP is still being outraised by the Senate Leadership Fund, the GOP’s top Senate super PAC, in large part thanks to billionaire Elon Musk and other Republican megadonors. Musk gave $158 million to SLF in the third quarter , according to its most recent FEC report, and the super PAC in turn sent that money to Texas’ Senate race in order to boost the scandal-plagued GOP nominee Ken Paxton. As of Sept. 30, SLF had raised more than $423 million for the cycle. Democrats have been able to offset much of Republicans’ super PAC cash advantage on the airwaves because of stronger candidate fundraising. But Republicans still have the advantage of a favorable map — and more outside money — as they hope to maintain control of at least one chamber of Congress next month.
sources.headline: Democrats’ top Senate super PAC has raised $354M this year

stories.headline: New York City votes to end horse-drawn carriages, with a phaseout through 2028

sources.body: GOODBYE HORSES: New York City isn’t horsing around anymore. The City Council voted overwhelmingly today to abolish the Big Apple’s horse carriage industry, handing a historic win to animal rights activists who’ve pushed to end the tourist attraction for decades. The vote doesn’t mean the industry sunsets overnight, though. The bill enacting the ban — which passed the Council with 40 yays, 7 nays and 2 abstentions — allows the roughly 200 carriage drivers who shuttle tourists around Central Park to continue operating until June 2028, when the industry will be reined into a legal halt officially. Council Speaker Julie Menin, who started making the legislation’s passage a priority over the summer, told reporters before the vote that the carriage horse-related June death of Romanch Mahajan , an 18-year-old Indian tourist, was the last straw. But she also cited a long record of horses dying in the streets as part of the reason for the bill finally crossing the finish line. “This has been a long time coming,” she said. Mayor Zohran Mamdani — who initially withheld support for the measure over labor protection concerns — got behind it earlier this month, sealing the deal for it to become law. He hasn’t yet set a date for signing the bill. Mamdani came on board after the Council modified the bill to give drivers pathways into other lines of work, and the phase-out period is key in that pursuit. Under the bill, the city must create a workforce transition program under which drivers would, between now and 2028, receive career counseling as well as referrals to employment opportunities in both public and private sectors, including with the Metropolitan Transportation Authority and hospitality and tourism outfits. The bill would also prohibit drivers from sending their horses to slaughter or using them for carriage duties in another city where it’s allowed. Horse carriage drivers and their supporters remain furious. The Transport Workers Union, which advocates for carriage drivers, announced yesterday that it will file a lawsuit to block the ban, arguing it violates federal and state laws. The union is especially incensed that the bill doesn’t require the city to pay out drivers for the value of their carriage licenses — an omission lawyers for the TWU say flies in the face of the Fifth Amendment’s prohibition on government usurping private property without compensation. Just as the Council was getting ready to vote, carriage supporters received backing from a somewhat unexpected source: President Donald Trump. “So sad to see the beloved Central Park Horse-drawn Carriage Industry ending after over a Century, based largely on one tragic accident,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post , referring to Mahajan. “When there is a car accident in the area, of which there are many, they don’t stop cars from entering the Park. So why would they stop the Carriages? It was a Great Tradition.” Also before today’s vote, dozens of TWU reps and carriage drivers gathered outside City Hall to blast the Council for moving forward with the legislation. One of them brought along a ziplock bag of equine feces with a handwritten label on it reading: “This is horse sh*t.” Christina Hansen, who’s been driving carriages for more than a decade, said she feels “disrespected” by the fact that the bill doesn’t guarantee she and her colleagues will be compensated for their licenses, which are worth hundreds of thousands of dollars. “There are people who are owed money on medallions, who have planned families, had children, bought houses, taken out loans,” Hansen said. “What’s going to happen to them?” Fellow carriage driver Danielle Slot, who voted for Mamdani in last year’s mayoral election, told Playbook she feels betrayed by his decision to back the bill without a provision mandating medallion reimbursement. “You say you’re going after billionaires, but you’re really going after the underdogs,” Slot said. “These guys are hardworking, every single medallion is its own independent business, and many are immigrant owned. I expected better from Mamdani than to be a puppet.” When asked why the bill only requires the city to “consider” medallion compensation as opposed to requiring it, Menin pointed a finger at the mayor. “To be clear, that was language that, you know, was worked out with the administration,” she told reporters at City Hall. Dora Pekec, a spokesperson for the mayor, did not dispute Menin’s account, but said the administration is “in discussions” about compensation for medallion owners. Mayors and Council speakers have tried to outlaw the industry since at least 2007. Momentum has built for a ban following tragic incidents in which horses have died or been severely injured in and around Central Park. But until now, those efforts have fizzled, in part because of political pressure from the Transport Workers Union. Carriage industry supporters argue that it can be reformed to ensure better safety standards without outlawing it outright. Council member Jim Gennaro, who introduced a bill that would do just that, said he believes Menin is at least partially politically motivated, pointing to the influence of NYCLASS, one of the main animal rights groups behind the push for a ban. “NYCLASS does have the ability to turn winners and losers in mayoral elections and in borough elections, and I don’t think that fact has been lost on the speaker,” he said before voting against the bill. NYCLASS notably tanked former Council Speaker Christine Quinn’s 2013 mayoral bid by spending heavily against her because of her reluctance to support a carriage ban at the time. Before the bill passed this afternoon, Gennaro tried to force through an amendment that would’ve delayed the phase-out deadline for the carriage industry until 2030, but it was rejected. On the other side of the bitter debate, supporters of the bill gathered for a rally in City Hall Park before the vote. Among them were members of Mahajan’s family, who have been fighting for the legislation since his death. “True justice means recognizing that these gentle, majestic horses do not belong on the congested asphalt,” Gaurav Mahajan, Romanch’s uncle, said. “By granting them the peaceful, green pastures they so deeply deserve, we fulfill Romanch’s purpose.” — Molly Reinmann and Chris Sommerfeldt  From the Capitol RAILING AGAINST ALBANY: As Planet Albany denizens may have noticed, the Office of General Services this week began installing hand railings down the middle of several staircases near the state Senate chamber. More railings are planned for the Assembly chamber-side stairs too. The project costs some $700,000 , per WNYC’s Jon Campbell — further evidence that the most expensive government building construction project of the 19th century is never really done. Aside from the cost, it’s an aesthetic change to a building teeming with history and one that is rarely altered. Historian and former state Assemblymember Jack McEneny is taking the latest addition to the New York state Capitol in stride. “I always thought it was only a matter of time that somebody would decide to do something,” he said in an interview when asked about the railings. McEneny is an expert on the building and has given guided tours. He noted the staircases were not built with safety in mind. “It was inevitable,” he said of adding the railings. “There’s a number of things that we did back two or three generations before that we wouldn’t do today.” The stone staircases in the Capitol are indeed steep and very hard. (Fifteen years ago, your Playbook writer landed on his face while sprinting from the second to the third floor, necessitating an emergency dental intervention.) The building, of course, has been altered over the years to fit the needs of people who work in it. That includes the installation of a small, hideaway elevator , which was used by a wheelchair-bound Franklin Roosevelt when he was governor. “We require more things than we did at the time of its opening,” McEneny said. “We also have more attorneys who will sue.” — Nick Reisman  FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL BLAKEMAN GROUP GETS $2M: The main super PAC supporting Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman has received $2 million from a dark money group created to back Donald Trump’s 2024 presidential bid. Securing American Greatness made the donation Tuesday to Strong and Safe New York, according to a filing submitted to the state Board of Elections. That group was formed by longtime Trump ally Taylor Budowich. The pro-Blakeman group has now raised $10.3 million since July. That makes it the largest single independent expenditure group so far this election cycle, though a longer roster of outside spenders boosting Gov. Kathy Hochul means she’s still the beneficiary of more super PAC money. — Bill Mahoney BROOKLYN BATTLE: The New York State Court of Appeals declined to weigh in Thursday on the long-running legal battle between factions of Brooklyn Democrats looking to lead the county party. State Assemblymember Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn, the former chair of the party, appealed a lower court’s decision that an August vote to change the makeup of the organization’s executive committee was invalid. The lower court’s ruling remains in effect after the appeals court decided not to take it up. The issue of if state Assemblymember Nikki Lucas, Bichotte Hermelyn’s successor of choice, was properly elected is still playing out in the courts. — Madison Fernandez  GOV AND MAYOR: Hochul’s campaign today released a video co-starring Mamdani as they prepare to hit the trail together for her reelection. The video highlighted their shared push for expanding child care, visiting a family that benefits from the service. POLITICO first reported this morning that the governor and mayor will make two appearances together in the coming days with events on Friday and Sunday in Brooklyn. — Nick Reisman FROM CITY HALL MAM LEANS ON MENIN: Mamdani put public pressure on Menin today by showing up to a rally calling for the passage of labor legislation that she hasn’t thrown her weight behind yet — in part because of legal concerns. The Delivery Protection Act, which was introduced by democratic socialist Council member Tiffany Cabán, would require Amazon and other retail giants to hire their own delivery workers. Currently, retailers can subcontract delivery employees via third party entities — a system that supporters of Cabán’s bill argue hampers workers’ ability to unionize and allows companies like Amazon to skirt accountability for labor violations. Thirty-four of the Council’s 51 members have signed on as co-sponsors of Cabán’s bill, giving it a veto-proof majority of support, and a hearing was held on it in April. But Menin hasn’t scheduled a vote on the measure or offered support for it, even though she was a co-sponsor of a version of the legislation last year before becoming speaker. Against that backdrop, Mamdani appeared on the steps of City Hall this morning with Cabán and other backers of the bill. In prepared remarks, he didn’t call out Menin by name, but blasted Amazon for pumping millions of dollars into lobbying against the bill. “Corporations like Amazon operate on a model of exploitation, and they are spending millions of dollars to convince New Yorkers otherwise,” he said. “But it will not work because we are here together today to make clear that we are going to pass the Delivery Protection Act.” By contrast, International Brotherhood of Teamsters General President Sean O’Brien, whose union represents Amazon workers, took direct aim at Menin, saying she must call a vote on the bill immediately. “Now is the time to get off your ass,” said O’Brien, who met privately with Mamdani before the rally. When asked later in the day why she isn’t immediately moving forward with the bill, Menin cited concerns she said need to be worked out regarding potential job losses that could come from barring Amazon from relying on third party contractors. But she also said Mamdani’s own Law Department had reached out to the Council with “legal concerns” with the bill that needed to be resolved before a vote. Menin didn’t elaborate on the legal issues. But a person with knowledge of the conversations between the Council and the Law Department, who was granted anonymity to discuss the ongoing talks, told Playbook one of the concerns is centered around ensuring the bill satisfies the high legal standard required for the city to mandate direct hiring in the private sector. A Mamdani spokesperson didn’t immediately return a request for comment on the legal concerns. Amazon spokesperson Steve Kelly pushed back against the criticism from Mamdani and O’Brien, saying the reliance on third parties “works because local entrepreneurs — people rooted in their communities — deliver a better experience.” “And this model isn't unusual — it's how businesses and governments operate every day,” Kelly said. “New York City routinely contracts with outside companies to build its infrastructure, run its school buses, and deliver social services. This legislation would single out one industry for restrictions the city doesn't even apply to its own operations.” It’s a bit unusual for Mamdani to put the speaker on public notice like this over Council legislation. So far in his mayoral term, he hasn’t leaned heavily into legislative battles in the chamber over bills that are still under consideration. — Chris Sommerfeldt  IN OTHER NEWS — DOUBLE AGENT: A campaign website for Thomas Kenny, an upstate Assembly candidate running on the Working Families Party ballot line, was created by an aide for Kenny’s ostensible opponent, Republican Allen Caruso. stories.headline: Georgia Republicans look to wealthy gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson to avert a broader midterm defeat

sources.body: Georgia Republicans are counting on Rick Jackson to save them from a wipeout in November — if President Donald Trump doesn’t get in the way. The billionaire health care executive and political newcomer has spent nearly $200 million since he entered the Georgia governor’s race earlier this year. That’s boosted GOP hopes as many in the party have all but given up on the state’s marquee Senate race, where Rep. Mike Collins is struggling to close the gap against a formidably well-funded Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff. Republicans worry that their open contests for attorney general and lieutenant governor as well as control of the state general assembly could be in peril in a larger blue wave. But Jackson’s deep pockets are being tested against a difficult political environment for Republicans, weighed down by unpopular Trump actions, including the war in Iran. And some in the GOP worry that the president’s repeated visits to Georgia could only make the situation worse. “I don't know that Trump coming helps Republicans more so than it excites Democrats, especially in a wave election year, and so becomes and becomes a catch-22 for Republican candidates,” said Jason Shepherd, a former Cobb County chair who is supporting Jackson. One Georgia-based Republican strategist who is not involved in the gubernatorial race posited that Trump’s dual appearances in the state almost certainly did more harm than help. They, like others in this article, were granted anonymity to speak openly about the race to avoid reprisals. “Every piece of data that I've seen, it is not MAGA Republicans that are unmotivated to vote in this election,” the person said. “All the data that I've seen is that the undecideds in our marquee races, and specifically in the governor's race, have a very, very negative opinion of the president. So, I can't really rationalize a case for how it would be helpful.” Jackson, for his part, has carefully navigated his relationship with the president and has not publicly broken with him on policy like other battleground Republicans. But he has not mentioned the president in any of the nearly 150 ads he’s run in the general election, according to an analysis of data from tracking firm AdImpact. Shortly after the RNC announced that Trump would return to the state this weekend, Jackson’s team said in a statement that the candidate will be campaigning in a different part of Georgia. And during his only televised gubernatorial debate on Oct. 6 against Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, Jackson never name-dropped the president — despite his opponent invoking Trump’s name eight times. Instead, the Republican mentioned popular outgoing GOP Gov. Brian Kemp five times and focused on Bottoms’ tenure as mayor of Atlanta during the Covid-19 pandemic. “It’s been proven time and again that when the message is on Georgia, and the results under Brian Kemp and the conservative vision and road map that's been laid out here, that we win in Georgia. When the focus is on D.C. and personal politics, we lose,” said Cole Muzio, president of the conservative Frontline Policy Action group .  The Jackson campaign declined to comment for this story. “President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party,” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement. Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, said in a statement that Republicans “are laser focused on winning, and our candidates will run the races necessary to best represent their districts and prevent Democrats from taking control." Jackson is one of several Republicans across the country who now must balance between keeping the president close enough to turn out Republican base voters, but not so closely as to alienate the center. Though many Georgia Republicans see Jackson as their de-facto ticket-topper, they don’t see his win as a guarantee against Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor, in a finicky battleground state like Georgia. Jackson has outspent Bottoms nearly 5-to-1 in the final stretch of the race but still remains in a close race in public polling . And yet, without him, Republicans fear the bottom would have already fallen out on races up and down the ballot, given how poorly Collins is performing in polls against Ossoff. Republicans’ top Senate super PAC, Senate Leadership Fund, was dark in Georgia last week , a sign the race may be slipping out of reach. “If Rick Jackson weren't running, we would all be in a lot of trouble,” said Stephen Lawson, a Georgia-based Republican strategist and Jackson ally. “He’s our best hope at keeping the state red.” A second Georgia-based Republican strategist, who is working on other races in the state, underscored how Jackson’s money is keeping the party afloat. “There is no question in my mind that without the extra $150 million he spent in his general election, that the ticket would be lost,” this person said. “That is the only reason there's still a fight to be had.” But, this person cautioned, the race is still very much a toss-up, and Jackson’s victory will rely on a large share of Georgia voters choosing to split their ballots between Ossoff for Senate and Jackson for governor. Jackson’s allies are optimistic that a significant number of voters will do just that. A private statewide poll reviewed by POLITICO found that roughly 19% of Georgia voters say they are definitely or likely to cast a vote for at least one Democrat and one Republican — a potentially significant pool of crossover voters that could power two very different results in the marquee contests. Whether the sheer force of Jackson’s spending will prove successful enough to overcome Trump is a microcosm of the larger issue his party is experiencing across the country: National Republicans, flush with cash, hold an enormous financial advantage over Democrats. But money alone may not be enough to insulate candidates in battlegrounds or even in traditionally red territory. “I don't know that Republicans across the country should feel as bullish about the cash influx that we've gotten because it didn't work here,” said the first GOP operative. “In terms of actively moving races in our favor, it at least didn't work here.” In the last month, as Bottoms began to spend more heavily on the air amid Jackson's spending advantage, her campaign has noted that polling has started to move marginally in her favor — even if the race remains largely within the margin of error . Her high name ID, as well as cash spent after the primary to define her early, are helping. “Rick Jackson has spent $200 million in this campaign but all the money in the world can’t hide the fact that he would be a lackey for Donald Trump,” TaNisha Cameron, a spokesperson for Bottoms, said in a statement. “Despite being outspent, Keisha’s message is breaking through and she has the momentum in this race right when it matters." Jackson is making more of an effort to tie himself closely to Kemp, who won over moderates and independents in his 2022 reelection for governor and has an approval rating that sits 30 points higher than the president’s in Georgia, according to a recent poll by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution . Kemp, for his part, has continued to be a presence on the trail for Jackson, including joining him on a statewide tour earlier this month and appearing in at least three TV ads for the campaign. But Jackson’s pathway to victory requires him to not only secure crossover voters that may support Ossoff in the Senate race or the type of voters who broke for Kemp, but also turn out the MAGA base who powered the president’s two presidential victories in the perennial battleground. The president is intent on still showing up for him. Shortly after Jackson dispatched Trump’s initially preferred candidate, Lt. Gov. Burt Jones, in June’s primary runoff, the president was quick to praise Jackson as standing “strong with ‘TRUMP.’” And in subsequent posts on Truth Social, Trump has called the health care executive a “good friend.” Trump, onstage Friday, called Jackson a “great businessman,” before adding: “I’ve been watching you, you are good, and he never did this before. He did it because he wants to straighten out things and he’s an amazing, an amazing story.” Aaron Pellish contributed to this report.
sources.headline: Rick Jackson is the GOP’s best hope in Georgia right now

sources.body: (ACN/Redacció) Els Mossos d’Esquadra han començat a desplegar l’anomenat pla Proa , destinat a prevenir i erradicar les bandes juvenils . Per aconseguir-ho, els Mossos, amb una col·laboració estreta de la Guàrdia Urbana —en el cas de Barcelona—, reforçaran la presència policial amb més agents en aquells punts on tenen constància de la presència d’aquest tipus d’organitzacions. L’impuls d’aquest pla arriba després de constatar un augment de la violència entre joves , especialment a Barcelona i la seva àrea metropolitana. També et pot interessar Manca de prevenció i masculinitat tòxica a xarxes: el còctel que ha reactivat les bandes juvenils Marina Segura i Vidal 3 minuts de lectura Barcelona concentra els incidents entre bandes Segons la radiografia territorial feta pels Mossos, el 66 % dels incidents estan protagonitzats per tres grups: Trinitarios, Barrio 18 i Los 300 . El 80 % dels incidents impliquen set bandes, els tres anteriors i quatre més: Latin Kings, PGS, Lobos i Mara Salvatrucha. Actuen sobretot a Barcelona i el seu entorn, però també hi ha ramificacions al Camp de Tarragona, Girona i Lleida. Encara no hi ha xifres gaire precises de la problemàtica, i aquest és un dels objectius del pla. A més, es vol prevenir que el problema creixi, especialment davant l’augment d’armes blanques i de foc als carrers. De fet, en els últims dos anys els Mossos atribueixen a aquests grups almenys tres homicidis. També et pot interessar La mort del menor a la Sagrera “no és casual” i els Mossos apunten a una disputa entre bandes Maria Solans 2 minuts de lectura De les bandes llatines a una realitat més complexa La diagnosi elaborada pels Mossos d’Esquadra constata una evolució clara del fenomen de les anomenades bandes llatines , que van emergir durant la primera dècada dels 2000. Si en aquell moment predominaven estructures formades per joves llatinoamericans, sobretot equatorians, i amb una forta simbologia importada de l’Amèrica Llatina i dels Estats Units, la realitat actual és diferent . Els grups actuals estan formats per joves d’origen divers , la majoria nascuts aquí però de família immigrant, sobretot llatinoamericana, però també n’hi ha d’origen espanyol, magrebí o xinès. Tenen lideratges variables, una organització flexible, i unes relacions internes i externes menys formals, jeràrquiques i rígides. El domini territorial continua sent un element central i motor de la violència, igual que la identitat, que comporta una lleialtat i obediència al grup, així com la realització de fets delictius, principalment tràfic de drogues i robatoris violents . Ara tenen més visibilitat, cosa que genera problemes de convivència i percepció d’inseguretat . Aquesta evolució fa necessari adaptar constantment les estratègies policials. També et pot interessar Per què la gent se sent insegura si els delictes baixen? Els experts alerten del paper de les xarxes Núria Granados 2 minuts de lectura Intel·ligència policial per anticipar-se El pla Proa articula una resposta transversal que integra la prevenció, la detecció, la investigació i la neutralització sota una mateixa direcció estratègica. A més, estableix un model de gestió integrada que permetrà centralitzar, analitzar i explotar la informació procedent de tot el territori per transformar-la en intel·ligència policial. L’objectiu és aprofundir en el coneixement dels membres vinculats als grups, les seves estructures, els lideratges, les connexions existents entre organitzacions i els espais on exerceixen influència, amb la finalitat d’anticipar-ne l’activitat i orientar les actuacions policials.
sources.headline: Pla de xoc dels Mossos contra les bandes juvenils: n’han detectat 34 amb un miler de membres

sources.body:
A Catalunya hi ha 34 grups juvenils violents , segons els Mossos d'Esquadra. El cos policial assegura que els tenen identificats, juntament amb un miler de persones que hi tindrien relació d'una manera o altra.

El seu tret més característic és la violència i, segons els Mossos, hi ha tres bandes principals: els Trinitarios, Barrio 18 i Los 300. Per mirar de desarticular-los, els Mossos posaran en marxa al novembre el Pla Proa .

Segons explica el cos policial, la mitjana d'edat dels membres d'aquests grups és d'uns 20 anys , aproximadament. Tot i això, es tracta d'un fenomen format tant per menors com per joves majors d'edat. "No tots els fets delictius que passen amb menors d'edat operen amb aquests grups violents", aclareix la comissarà en cap dels Mossos d'Esquadra, Sílvia Catà.

Els Mossos atribueixen als grups juvenil violents almenys tres homicidis en els últims anys. Un dels quals és l'assassinat a trets d'un menor a Barcelona aquest juliol. S'investiga com un possible enfrontament entre bandes rivals.

Els principals delictes que cometen, segons els Mossos, són agressions , càstigs entre ells, baralles , lesions, robatoris, tràfic de drogues, tinença d'arma blanca i, de vegades, arma de foc.

El 66% dels delictes d'aquests 34 grups juvenils violents identificats els fan els grups més actius: els Trinitarios , Barrio 18 i Los 300; de manera que tres de cada quatre membres són d'aquests tres grups principals.

Operen, sobretot, a Barcelona i a l'àrea metropolitana , amb ramificacions al Camp de Tarragona, Girona i Lleida.

A diferència de les bandes llatines que van proliferar fa anys, els grups violents juvenils actuals no s'identifiquen per la nacionalitat . Durant la primera dècada dels anys 2000, predominaven les estructures jerarquitzades i un dels principals vincles era l'origen, principalment de països llatinoamericans. També disposaven d'una simbologia que els identificava.

El fenomen actual, en canvi, té una naturalesa multicultural, segons concreten els Mossos . La majoria dels integrants han nascut a Catalunya. En canvi, el sentiment de pertinença al grup s'articula a través de la violència i del domini territorial .

Per això, el pla preveu augmentar el patrullatge en determinats espais com places o línies de metro.

Tot i aquestes diferències, coincideixen en la voluntat de mantenir l'estatus dins del grup i la rivalitat amb grups contraris .

La policia catalana encara no disposa de xifres precises sobre aquesta nova realitat, però han detectat que tenen una gran capacitat de creixement i accés a armes blanques i, en menor mesura, també de foc .

"Preocupen perquè són grups on hi ha menors, molts joves i per la violència extrema que moltes vegades opera entre grups", ha manifestat la comissària Catà.

De cara al novembre, els Mossos d'Esquadra posaran en marxa el Pla Proa , amb dos objectius concrets: desarticular els grups juvenils violents i fer prevenció perquè no n'hi hagi de nous.

Es tracta, a diferència de l'abordatge de les bandes llatines dels anys 2000, d'una estratègia més transversal que integrarà la prevenció, la detecció, la investigació i la neutralització sota una mateixa direcció estratègica.

Amigos del joven asesinado en el parque de la Pegaso de barcelona ecuerdan a su compañero en el lugar del crimen 

Cuatro encapuchados se acercaron el pasado 2 de julio a un joven de 15 años que se encontraba con varios familiares en el parque de la Pegaso, en el barrio barcelonés de Sant Andreu, y le descerrajaron varios disparos. El menor, de origen colombiano y residente en Catalunya desde hacía apenas siete meses, murió en el acto. El crimen, vinculado a las bandas latinas, puso de manifiesto el resurgimiento de estos grupos en Catalunya, un fenómeno que ya tuvo especial incidencia entre los años 2000 y 2015.

En la actualidad, los Mossos d’Esquadra tienen identificados 34 grupos violentos activos en Catalunya que se dedican al tráfico de drogas, agresiones e incluso homicidios. Entre los más numerosos figuran los Trinitarios, Barrio 18, los 300– estos tres son los mayoritarios– mientras que también han detectado la presencia de otros grupos como los Latin Kings, los PGS (los Pegaso), los Lobos y la Mara Salvatrucha. Aunque la mayor concentración se encuentra en Barcelona y su área metropolitana, la policía también ha hallado ramificaciones en Tarragona, Girona y Lleida.

Los Mossos han puesto en marcha un plan para atajar un fenómeno que no está desbocado pero que ha generado los primeros brotes de violencia y que temen que en un contexto de presencia masiva de armas blancas y de fuego puede llegar a estallar. El plan prevé una actuación coordinada con los diferentes cuerpos policiales del territorio para mejorar el conocimiento del fenómeno y detectar de forma temprana la aparición de nuevos grupos.

“Se trata de personas muy jóvenes, algunas de ellas menores de edad, que cometen hechos delictivos, especialmente con armas blancas y, en ocasiones, también con armas de fuego, lo que genera mucha inseguridad entre la ciudadanía en Cataluña. El plan tiene dos objetivos principales: por un lado, eliminar los 34 grupos juveniles que actualmente ya están asentados en Cataluña y, por otro, erradicar e imposibilitar que otras bandas violentas operen en el territorio”, indicó este jueves la comisaria jefa de los Mossos, Sílvia Catà.

Los primeros indicios de este repunte aparecieron a mediados de 2024. Durante las noches de los fines de semana se registraron diversos episodios violentos, como por ejemplo en el Metro de Barcelona, protagonizados por jóvenes, en su mayoría catalanes de origen latinoamericano, implicados en peleas con machetes y otras armas blancas. En mayo de este año, los Mossos y la Guardia Urbana de Barcelona desarticularon una parte de Los 300, una organización integrada por 18 jóvenes, seis de ellos menores de edad, presuntamente dedicada a cometer robos violentos con cuchillos y machetes y al tráfico de drogas. Además, a algunos de sus miembros se les atribuye un intento de homicidio.

Los Mossos calculan que en Barcelona hay alrededor de 1.000 jóvenes vinculados a alguna banda latina y, de estos, unos 400 que ejercen un papel activo. No obstante, destacan que estas organizaciones presentan características distintas a las de hace dos décadas. “El fenómeno de expansión del 2000 consistió en exportar las bandas latinas del país de origen con el objetivo de luchar contra una organización rival. El sentimiento de identidad se forjaba al tener un adversario. Ahora, como todos los integrantes son nacionales, esto queda desdibujado”, explica el subjefe de los Mossos, el comisario Ramon Chacón. “Si ponemos la rivalidad y la potencia que mantenían estos grupos hace 20 años y le añadimos las armas blancas y de fuego que hay en la calle, el escenario cambia totalmente y es preocupante”.

sources.body: Barcelona té ara mateix 15 dipòsits de recollida d’aigües pluvials arreu de la ciutat que, en episodis de pluges torrencials , poden emmagatzemar fins a 450.000 metres cúbics —450 milions de litres d’aigua— al subsol i evitar que inundi la superfície urbana . Per primera vegada, tots 15 dipòsits van funcionar al 100 % durant l’ episodi de pluges del cap de setmana del 3 i 4 d’octubre , en què es van omplir i buidar dues vegades i mitja , en conjunt. També et pot interessar Aiguats forts: com es gestionen per evitar inundacions a Barcelona Joaquim Serra 2 minuts de lectura El primer dipòsit en 15 anys Aquesta xarxa va començar-se a crear fa dècades , i la darrera peça a incorporar-se va ser el 2013, amb el dipòsit de les Rieres d’Horta , que té una capacitat per emmagatzemar uns 90.000 metres cúbics d’aigua. Segons ha avançat la tinenta d’alcaldia d’Urbanisme i Acció Climàtica, Laia Bonet , això canviarà el 2028 amb l’entrada en funcionament el dipòsit de la rambla de Prim , a tocar de la Via Trajana, al districte de Sant Martí. Tindrà una capacitat per retenir i controlar prop de 100.000 metres cúbics d’aigua de pluja. Es tracta d’un dipòsit executat al 50 % i que, segons Bonet, se suma a la xarxa “després de 15 anys sense haver-ne construït cap altre “. En paral·lel, la tinenta d’alcaldia ha assenyalat que “també estem treballant en els projectes dels dipòsits de Bac de Roda, de la Sagrera —per donar servei a la futura estació— i de Vallcarca —per evitar inundacions a la futura rambla verda. L’Ajuntament invertirà aquest mandat uns 200 milions d’euros per ampliar la xarxa actual, de 15 dipòsits amb, almenys, quatre basses subterrànies més properament, fins acabar-la de completar amb 29 dipòsits més . En aquest sentit, el Pla director integral del sanejament de Barcelona preveu la reserva de sòl per anar avançant. Interior del vas inferior del dipòsit de Joan Miró Dipòsits per tres funcions Els 15 dipòsits actuals estan repartits en punts estratègics per abastar , localment, diversos punts de la ciutat . En aquest sentit, hi ha tres categories de dipòsit, en funció de la seva finalitat: A les zones altes : tenen la missió principal de retenir l’aigua a les cotes altes de la ciutat, per impedir que s’inundi la part de la ciutat a cotes més baixes. A les zones baixes : tenen la missió principal de retenir l’aigua a les cotes baixes de la ciutat, per impedir que l’aigua arribi, bruta, al mar o als rius i sense haver passat abans per una depuradora. A les zones intermèdies : tenen la missió de combinar les dues funcions anteriors, i anar-se adaptant en funció de com es desenvolupi un episodi de pluges. Una peça més en el disseny de la ciutat que ha de prevenir inundacions és que en superfície sigui cada cop més permeable . Així, una altra de les actuacions que es duen a terme —en paral·lel a la projecció de dipòsits d’aigües pluvials— és la creació dels sistemes urbans de drenatge sostenible (SUDS), que darrerament s’han triplicat . També et pot interessar Barcelona triplica els espais que absorbeixen l’aigua de pluja i ja suma 17 hectàrees Lluís Cruz Berasategui 3 minuts de lectura

Visita al depósito pluvial del parque de Joan Miró, que se llenó durante los aguaceros del 3 y 4 de octubre / JORDI OTIX / VÍDEO: J. OTIX / M. TUDELA

La intensidad nunca vista en Barcelona de las precipitaciones caídas el fin de semana del 3 y 4 de octubre ha vuelto a poner sobre la mesa el debate acerca de la capacidad que tiene la ciudad para soportar unos aguaceros que serán cada vez más frecuentes . Durante el episodio del primer fin de semana de octubre y en términos globales, los depósitos tuvieron que vaciarse y llenarse dos veces y media. Entre las 9 de la mañana del día 3 y la misma hora del día 4, nueve de los quince enormes tanques de agua rebasaron su capacidad . En este sentido, la función de la red de depósitos pluviales municipales resulta "clave para minimizar las afectaciones", ha indicado la teniente de Alcaldía Laia Bonet este jueves, desde el interior del depósito situado bajo el parque de Joan Miró. La infraestructura es gigantesca: casi 20 metros de profundidad (como un edificio de seis plantas), una capacidad de 55.000 m³ ("unas 25 piscinas olímpicas", ha detallado Bonet) y un bosque de centenares de columnas de alrededor de un metro de diámetro pueblan los dos cuerpos de que dispone la infraestructura para retener el agua de lluvia: "Esto es como una catedral ", ha comparado Bonet.

"No tenemos registros en Barcelona en que los depósitos hayan tenido que gestionar una lluvia de esa intensidad y con esa duración, fue una precipitación histórica, fuera de lugar ", describe Alejandro Ortiz, director de la empresa pública Barcelona Cicle de l'Aigua (BCASA). Pese a que el sistema funcionó, Ortiz ha asegurado este jueves que los técnicos "sufrieron porque se enfrentaban a una situación muy delicada" . La inauguración, prevista para el año 2028, del nuevo depósito de la Rambla Prim, será la primera de una infraestructura de este tipo que Barcelona estrena desde el año 2013, cuando abrió el depósito de Rieres d'Horta. El presupuesto de su construcción alcanza los 60 millones de euros: "No nos podemos permitir este lapso de tiempo entre una infraestructura y otra", ha indicado Bonet, quien ha asegurado que "se está acelerando" la construcción de nuevos depósitos.

Interior del depósito pluvial municipal situado bajo el parque de Joan Miró, este 22 de octubre de 2026 / Jordi Otix / EPC

El de la Rambla Prim será un gran depósito, aunque no el más grande de la ciudad. Sus 60.000 m³ previstos de capacidad lo situarán al mismo nivel del localizado en el parque de Joan Miró, pero no alcanzará los 100.000 m³ del que está situado en la Zona Universitaria, el más grande de la ciudad . Bonet ha detallado que no será el único, aunque el resto de los que están en marcha dependen de otras operaciones urbanísticas. Así, en los próximos años se construirán también en La Sagrera (vinculado a la construcción de la nueva estación) y en Vallcarca (relacionado con la futura Rambla Verda) . Además, el Ayuntamiento ya dispone de la reserva de suelo para hacer realidad otros 25 depósitos y ultima la puesta en marcha del colector de aguas de la avenida Diagonal, obra estrechamente relacionada con la conexión de las líneas de TRAM. En total, y cuando se finalicen todos ellos, la capacidad de la ciudad de Barcelona para gestionar el agua de lluvia en los episodios intensos se triplicará : si actualmente son 477.000 los metros cúbicos que aúnan los 15 depósitos actuales, en el futuro se sumará un millón de metros cúbicos más.
sources.headline: Barcelona construye su primer depósito pluvial tras 15 años de cara a estrenarlo en 2028

La estación de Gornal de FGC, este jueves. / EL PERIÓDICO

Dos días después del desprendimiento de parte del techo del túnel de Gornal , en L'Hospitalet de Llobregat (Barcelona), Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat de Catalunya (FGC) sigue sin fijar una fecha para restablecer la circulación habitual de la R5, R6, S8 y S3 de la Línea Llobregat-Anoia, afectadas desde el incidente y cuyos trenes continúan circulando por vía única en ese tramo.

La incidencia, registrada a última hora de la tarde de este martes, fue inspeccionada por técnicos de Adif y FGC , que analizaron las causas del derrumbe para determinar cómo repararlo y restablecer la red. Y, aunque inicialmente se barajó que el incidente podría estar relacionado con las vías de Adif situada justo encima del túnel, las primeras investigaciones descartan que la infraestructura de la entidad pública estatal fuera la causante , según han informado fuentes de la compañía ferroviaria a EL PERIÓDICO.

De hecho, el servicio de Rodalies de l a R2Sud y los Regionals de Tarragona y Lleida , que circulan a nivel de superfície por encima del túnel de FGC, no se ha visto resentido en ningún momento de la semana por esta incidencia en concreto. En este punto de L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, además de los trenes de Rodalies y del túnel de FGC, existe una galería situada a más profundidad por donde avanzan los trenes de alta velocidad entre Barcelona y Madrid. La construcción de esta última infraestructura, hace ahora 20 años, provocó graves afectaciones y obligó a interrumpir el servicio tanto de Rodalies como de FGC alguna semana. Fuentes de Adif, sin embargo, descartan que la situación actual tenga relación alguna con el túnel de la alta velocidad.

Las afectaciones en la red de Ferrocarrils no son menores. En concreto, la R5 (Manresa) y la R6 (Igualada) han quedado reducidas a dos trenes por hora y sentido y circulan solo hasta y desde L'Hospitalt-Av. Carrilet, por lo que pierden la llegada habitual hasta Plaça España. Por otro lado, la línea S3 (Can Ros) todavía ha quedado más recortada en frecuencia, con un tren por hora y con las mismas condiciones que las anteriores, y para poder continuar hasta Barcelona FGC ha recomendado usar el metro. La que menos afectaciones ha tenido ha sido la S8 (Martorell), que mantiene el servicio hasta y desde Plaça Espanya con una frecuencia aproximada de 15 minutos.

Los trabajos se centran ahora en estabilizar la zona afectada y garantizar que la infraestructura reúne todas las condiciones de seguridad necesarias antes de volver a utilizar las dos vías. Por el momento, FGC no ha concretado cuánto tiempo pueden prolongarse estas actuaciones ni cuándo podrá recuperarse el servicio habitual. Ante esa incógnita, la compañía ha señalado que las novedades sobre la evolución de los trabajos y el restablecimiento de la circulación se comunicarán a través de sus canales oficiales . Hasta entonces, los usuarios deberán continuar consultando el estado del servicio antes de viajar y prever posibles incrementos en los tiempos de desplazamiento.

Aquesta matinada s'ha desconvocat la vaga d'autobusos de Barcelona , que preveia aturades aquest dimecres, dijous i cinc dies més aquest octubre.

La direcció de la companyia i els sindicats han pactat un nou conveni col·lectiu, que tindrà una vigència de quatre anys .

El preacord garanteix més dies de descans i preveu una reducció progressiva de la jornada laboral fins a les 35 hores setmanals.

L'any que ve, els treballadors de bus tindran 10 dies més de descans. Podran sumar tres dies més si es donen determinades condicions com l'absentisme o millores operatives que permetin aconseguir prou estalvis per contractar més personal.

També han aconseguit més dies de descans en cap de setmana.

L'acord també ha permès desconvocar les cinc jornades de protestes més que s'havien programat per a aquest mes.

🚍 Desconvocada la vaga de #busbcn de TMB 👉 La direcció de TMB i el comitè de vaga han arribat a un acord que ha portat els sindicats a desconvocar les aturades previstes avui dimecres i altres 5 dies del mes d'octubre ➕Info: https://t.co/OSILu3RTUM https://t.co/SQ0RiNgHvh

La plantilla d'autobusos de Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) estava convocada aquesta setmana a dues noves jornades de vagues parcials. La primera era aquest dimecres 14 i la intenció era repetir-la aquest dijous 15 d'octubre.

El Departament d'Empresa i Treball havia establert uns serveis mínims que oscil·laven entre el 40 i el 20%. Durant la resta de la jornada, es preveia que el servei fos l'habitual.

Les vagues parcials d'aquesta setmana formaven part de les set que el comitè d'empresa va anunciar per a aquest octubre després que al setembre no s'assolís cap acord entre l'empresa i els sindicats davant la demanda de millores laborals i salarials.

La primera va ser la setmana passada. Abans del preacord també n'hi havia de previstes per als dies 20, 22, 27 i 29 d'octubre.

Els treballadors del servei d'autobusos reclamaven millores en els calendaris laborals i la reducció de la jornada a 35 hores setmanals. Volien, a més, que s'apliquessin des del 2027 i no de manera diferida, com plantejava la direcció.

A més de canvis en el conveni com l' augment salarial , la millora de calendaris per a tots els col·lectius o el lot de Nadal , també denunciaven que no se'ls apliquen els dos dies de descans consecutius a la setmana que els pertoquen per llei.

Tant aquests descansos setmanals com la reducció de la jornada són les línies vermelles que la plantilla marcava en la negociació, segons el comitè d'empresa.

Dos trabajadores de Parques y Jardines con un vehículo de la empresa municipal, en el parque de Glòries, este verano pasado en Barcelona. / MANU MITRU

Como otros oficios que se ejercen al aire libre y exigen un esfuerzo físico, los jardineros de los parques públicos de Barcelona han sido uno de los colectivos de trabajadores que han estado expuestos a las temperaturas extremas del pasado verano en la ciudad. Empleados del Instituto Municipal de Parques y Jardines y otros servicios públicos recibieron unas pulseras térmicas con las que controlar la temperatura corporal para detectar el riesgo de originarse un golpe de calor y una instrucción del ayuntamiento estableció medidas de seguridad ante la canícula para la plantilla que trabaja a pie de calle . En todo caso, ambas medidas no han resuelto todas las carencias frente al tiempo cada vez más sofocante con que el personal municipal ha de capear, a tenor de una resolución reciente de la Inspecció de Treball. El organismo ha concluido que Parques y Jardines “ha establecido unas condiciones de trabajo que no cumplen con los requisitos mínimos de seguridad” , al contar con más de 100 vehículos que no están equipados con aire acondicionado.

A raíz de una denuncia de la sección sindical de CGT , la Inspecció de Treball ha requerido a la empresa del Ayuntamiento de Barcelona que corrija las "deficiencias detectadas y se garantice la seguridad y la salud de las personas trabajadoras en el uso de los equipos de trabajo y vehículos durante situaciones de climatología adversa por calor". Antes de tomar una resolución, el órgano reclamó este pasado verano a Parques y Jardines que le detallase qué unidades de la flota no disponen de climatización. La compañía facilitó un listado en el que figuran 105 matrículas de modelos sin aire acondicionado, según consta en el informe al que EL PERIÓDICO ha tenido acceso. En la relación aparecen 67 furgonetas, 27 camionetas, 10 camiones y un turismo, todos ellos faltos de aparatos de climatización .

La Inspecció de Treball plasma en el dictamen que “el motivo de que no tengan aire acondicionado, según exponen los representantes de la empresa, es que se adquirieron sin ningún tipo de sistema de climatización o porque son pequeños vehículos eléctricos que no soportan el consumo de aire acondicionado”. El organismo dio audiencia tanto a miembros de la sociedad municipal como a representantes de la plantilla. “Ambas partes han reconocido de forma explícita que las personas trabajadoras que hacen uso de los citados vehículos durante el periodo estival están sometidas a elevadas temperaturas dentro de los habitáculos de los mismos”.

El Ayuntamiento contesta que Parques y Jardines “ha impulsado una inversión para instalar aires acondicionados, hasta llegar al 58% de la flota ”. Añade que el órgano estudia “nuevos proyectos de inversión y medidas para llegar a más vehículos”. Los Comuns han emplazado esta semana al gobierno del PSC a priorizar que los vehículos de los servicios municipales se equipen con climatización.
